name: Torrents
tip: Folder torrents. A torrent's address is a key (nfolder1...), not a hash of its contents, so the publisher can add or remove files without the link ever changing. Tap one to see what's inside.

children.name: t_back
children.label: All torrents
children.tip: Back to the list of torrents.

children.name: t_manage
children.label: Manage
children.tip: Download everything, pin, copy the link, rescan or remove the open torrent.

children.name: torrents
children.empty: Nothing here yet - tap + to open a link or share a folder.
children.tip: Torrents you downloaded and torrents you publish. Tap one to open it; inside, tap a folder to go in, ".." to go up, or a file to open it.

name: Add
tip: Add a torrent: open somebody's link, or turn a folder on this device into one.

children.name: t_open_link
children.label: Open a link
children.tip: Paste an nfolder1... link (or an npub / hex id) to see what a torrent holds and download it.

children.name: t_add_disk
children.label: Share a folder
children.tip: Pick a directory on this device and turn it into a torrent. The files are served straight from disk - nothing is copied - and you hold its key, so only you can change what's in it.

name: Swarm
tip: Who else has the open torrent. The Indexers answer with devices, never with bytes - and they say enough about each device for the client to choose well.

children.name: swarm_refresh
children.label: Refresh
children.tip: Ask the Indexers again who is holding this folder.

children.name: swarm_log
children.label: Holders
children.tip: Best holder first: an awake machine on mains and a real uplink beats a phone on battery and a metered data plan. "direct" = we heard this device ourselves; "dht" = an Indexer told us.

name: Info
tip: The open torrent's share link and what it holds.

children.name: copy_link
children.label: Copy link
children.tip: Show and copy the nfolder1... link. It carries the folder key, a few provider hints and the publisher - the name is deliberately NOT in it, because an unsigned name in a link is a phishing surface.

children.name: copy_id
children.label: Copy id (hex)
children.tip: Copy the raw hex folder id.

children.name: info_log
children.label: Torrent info
children.tip: Link, file count, size, and how often this device has served its files.

name: Settings
tip: How this device behaves as a peer.

children.name: seeding
children.tip: Pinning is what makes a torrent survive: your device keeps a full copy and tells the Indexers it holds it, so the publisher's phone stops being the only source.

children.name: pin_on_open
children.label: Pin what I download
children.tip: After opening a link, keep a full copy and seed it. Turn this off to download without joining the swarm - it works, but a network of pure leechers holds nothing.

children.name: rescan_min
children.label: Rescan my folders every (minutes)
children.tip: How often a torrent shared from disk is re-scanned, so files you add or delete on disk are published to the swarm. 0 = never (rescan by hand from Manage).

children.name: settings_log
children.label: This device
children.tip: What this device is currently holding and serving.
